title: Golden Rice (NSIC Rc 682GR2E) Inbred Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Golden Rice (NSIC Rc 682GR2E) Rice: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: Golden Rice is NSIC Rc 682GR2E, an inbred rice for Philippine rice farms: about 118 days and 5.6 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 682GR2E is an inbred rice variety for Philippine rice farms, sold as Golden Rice or Malusog Rice and known locally as Malusog 1. The NSIC approved it in 2022. PhilRice and IRRI bred it. It matures in about 118 days and averages 5.6 tonnes per hectare, with a top yield of 5.8 tonnes in trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Golden Rice or Malusog Rice, or rice variety 682GR2E, this is the one. Compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 5.6 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 111 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 5.8 tonnes.
**Watch out for:** green leafhopper, sheath blight, tungro.
**Cooked rice:** low amylose, so soft and tender.

blocks.caption: Key facts of NSIC Rc 682GR2E (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 682GR2E yield?

On average it gives 5.6 tonnes per hectare. That is about 111 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 2 Philippine inbreds on the list, which is 6.2 tonnes. But the top yield, 5.8 tonnes, came from a trial with good water, seed and care. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 118 days from sowing to harvest. Varieties of 100 to 120 days count as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: So scout early for [green leafhopper](/pests/green-leafhopper), [sheath blight](/diseases/sheath-blight), [tungro](/diseases/rice-tungro). When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.
Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, Filipino taste has moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer.

The growing environment of this variety is not on record. So ask your municipal agriculturist whether it does well in your town, and read [how to pick the best rice variety for your area](/blog/best-rice-variety-for-my-area). For the right month, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is Golden Rice the same as NSIC Rc 682GR2E?
items.a: Yes. Golden Rice is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 682GR2E is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Malusog 1. The numbers on this page are for NSIC Rc 682GR2E.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 682GR2E?
items.a: It is known as Malusog 1. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 682GR2E take to harvest?
items.a: About 118 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 682GR2E?
items.a: It averages 5.6 tonnes per hectare, about 111 cavans of 50 kilograms. The best trial reached 5.8 tonnes. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In trials it was weak against green leafhopper, sheath blight, tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
